parts.gloss: that which is made to/passive nominalizer

literal: Those who possess, that which is called [possession], is zeal; those who do not have that, what they possess, do they possess [it] otherwise?
translation: That which is truly called a possession is one's inner zeal; as for those who lack it, do they really possess whatever else they may own?
modern: ஒருவர் பெற்றுள்ளார் என்று சொல்லத்தக்கது அவரிடம் உள்ள ஊக்கமே ஆகும்; அந்த ஊக்கம் இல்லாதவர்கள் வேறு எதை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், அவர்கள் எதையும் உடையவர் ஆவார்களோ?
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that inner energy or zeal (ūkkam) is the only true possession a person can have. The poet argues that if someone lacks this vital drive, any material wealth or other possessions they might hold are of no real value. The rhetorical question "do they really possess?" (uṭaiyarō) highlights that without motivation and willpower, external riches are as good as non-existent. Thus, the chapter on "possession of energy" begins by defining energy itself as the ultimate wealth.
